messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a weird p99 spike on route /chat/stream after yesterday's kernel routing tweak. p50/95 fine, p99 jumped from 420ms -> 1.6s for ~3% of requests.
jyoti: ugh. seeing the same in the route KPI card. throughput steady but long tail up. any correlation with KV warmups?
samir: I pulled a few traces. Lots of them show an extra 'kernel_misroute' hop: request routed to a kernel variant that triggers mv-copy path and forces KV reload.
liz: can you paste an example trace?
samir: sure — snippet from trace logs: ```trace_id=abc123 route=/chat/stream kernel_id=k_v1 -> k_v2 batch_wait_ms=12 kv_hit=false kernel_exec_ms=200 kv_load_ms=810 total_ms=1635```
jyoti: that kv_load_ms=810 is the offender. looks like we missed KV warmup for the fallback kernel.
alex: this is a telemetry gap — Console per-route KPI card only shows p50/p95/p99 and request rate. We need token-level waterfall breakdown (batch_wait / kernel_exec / kv_load / net).
perf-bot: perf-alert: route=/chat/stream p99 > 1500ms (3.1% of samples) detected at 2026-03-18T09:12:10Z
liz: +1 for token-level breakdown. also we should surface kernel_id tag and kv_hit in the KPI ingest so we can filter slices where kv_hit=false or kernel != preferred.
jyoti: proposal: add tags on telemetry: kernel_id, kernel_variant_reason (fallback|backoff|policy), batch_wait_ms, kv_hit, kv_load_ms. Then add new Console card: "Route token waterfall" with stacked p50/p95/p99 bars and ability to filter by kernel_id and kv_hit.
samir: implementation note: need to ensure continuous batching doesn't aggregate away batch_wait_ms samples. we should record per-request batch_wait_ms (sampled) and a batch_size histogram.
alex: also need a short-term fix: auto-warm KV on kernel handoff. maybe on routing fallback we kick async prefetch for top-k prefixes. ops-bot can we patch routing policy to prefetch?
ops-bot: created ticket #INF-2314: prefetch-on-fallback. assigned to infra-oncall. ETA 48h.
jyoti: for dashboards: add EXPLAIN button that surfaces 10 example traces contributing to p99 with the waterfall breakdown and kernel_id. That will help triage regressions quickly.
liz: +1. also add alert rule: if p99 increases by >2x AND kv_hit_rate drops by >10% for a route -> page oncall.
samir: FYI I ran a quick profile of a sample request in dev cluster: kernel selection path shows a 4ms decision cost but triggers expensive model weights remap on some kernels (costly on first request). snippet: ```prof: kernel_load_remap_ms=780 on k_v2 first_call=true```
ajex: (typo) alex: good catch. we should annotate first_call boolean in telemetry too.
jyoti: action items: 1) telemetry schema change (kernel_id, kv_hit, batch_wait_ms, kv_load_ms, first_call) — owner: jyoti 2) Console card prototype — owner: liz 3) routing prefetch ticket — ops-bot / infra-oncall 4) alert rule — owner: samir
alex: can we also add sampling to avoid cardinality explosion on kernel_id? maybe map kernel_id -> kernel_family tag for dashboard.
jyoti: yes, agree. kernel_family (e.g., float16-8bit, int8-q, fallback-compat) will be low-cardinality. include kernel_id for traces only.
liz: I'll sketch the UI tomorrow: stacked waterfall, split by kernel_family, toggle kv_hit filter, and a mini-trace viewer.
samir: I'll add instrumentation in the runtime to emit kv_hit and kv_load_ms when KV service is touched. will open PR and link here.
alex: thanks team. let's aim to ship telemetry + dashboard alpha in 2 sprints so we can detect and resolve these kernel-misroute regressions faster. :rocket:
